question: When using normal vectors to find a dihedral angle, what relationship may hold between the angle between the normal vectors and the plane angle of the dihedral angle?
solution: Depending on which sides of the half-planes the normal vectors point toward, the angle may equal the dihedral angle itself or its supplement.

edges.reason: The normal vector is defined geometrically as perpendicular to the plane. Direction vectors are a parallel idea and are useful for computation, but the conceptual criteria can be met through line-plane perpendicularity.
edges.scope: perpendicularity of normal to lines in the plane

edges.reason: Line and line-plane angles give an analogous practice in equal-or-supplementary reasoning. The angle between normals needs only the dot product cosine formula, not the line-angle node.
The source explicitly uses normals despite the broad English title Dihedral Angles.

The target is the angle between specified half-plane faces, not an arbitrary normal-vector angle. Its geometric object and common edge must be identifiable before interpreting the result. The actual target uses half-plane normals and must distinguish equal from supplementary normal angles. The geometric half-planes, edge and interior are necessary before interpreting that calculation.
edges.scope: Interpret the geometric angle computed by the corrected half-plane-normal procedure.
